findings.reason: The protected source uses the forbidden generic local name index for a bit position. The campaign standard requires conventional mathematical variables for such positions, and 1 << i communicates the mask relationship directly.

The inert candidate preserves the proven bitmask progress DP while enumerating each state as (mask, current), using i for the stick bit, and naming next_progress before the capacity check and modulo reset. This removes repeated table lookups and makes the state transition easier to explain without changing solve(matchsticks) or either asymptotic bound.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 473, its Python integer-array method, and its runnable solve(matchsticks) adapter. The candidate uses every physical stick at most once through its bit, accepts only a full-mask partition into four equal positive sums, and never splits a stick.

The protected app source and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2064977855 are algorithmically identical: both reject invalid totals and oversized sticks, store current-side progress per used-stick mask, append every fitting unused stick, reset progress modulo the target, and require a zero-progress full mask. The candidate changes only local naming and cached transition values and remains inert.

The legal 2-stick, 4-stick, and 8-stick workloads span 4x in the state-bit variable and exercise both fast rejection and subset exploration. The exact candidate passed all 10 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.17x the calibrated reference runtime. A correct unpruned four-side assignment control passed every opaque output but failed only performance at 41.53x the reference runtime.

The candidate-targeted Approach exactly defines progress[mask], the cached current value, 1 << i membership, next_progress capacity test, modulo side reset, full-mask condition, and fixed subset-sum argument. Its O(n * 2^n)-time and O(2^n)-space claims match both the candidate and the branch manifest.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves the use-all-sticks, no-breaking, exactly-once rules, both examples and explanations in order, both constraints, and the Example 1 square arrangement. An independent accessible table records the source image's three single length-2 sides and one side composed of the two length-1 sticks.
